questions.problem: Given the elliptic cone $\frac{(x-6)^{2}}{9}+\frac{(y-4)^{2}}{8}=\frac{(z+6)^{2}}{6},$ find its intercepts with the $y$-axis.
questions.worked_solution:
To find the $y$-intercepts of the elliptic cone, we plug $x=0$ and $z=0$ into the equation and solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(0-6)^{2}}{9}+\frac{(y-4)^{2}}{8} & =\frac{(0+6)^{2}}{6} \\ \frac{36}{9}+\frac{(y-4)^{2}}{8} & =\frac{36}{6} \\ 4+\frac{(y-4)^{2}}{8} & =6 \\ \frac{(y-4)^{2}}{8} & =2 \\ (y-4)^{2} & =16 \\ y-4 & =\pm 4 \\ y & =4\pm 4 \\ y & =0,8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intercepts with the $y$-axis are $(0,0,0)$ and $(0,8,0).$

questions.problem: What is the trace in the $xz$-plane of the elliptic cone $(x+1)^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{6}=(z-1)^{2}\,?$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the trace in the $xz$-plane, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the elliptic cone, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+1)^{2}+\frac{{0}^{2}}{6} & =(z-1)^{2} \\ (x+1)^{2} & =(z-1)^{2} \\ \pm (x+1) & =z-1 \\ z & =\pm (x+1)+1\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us two lines in the $xz$-plane with equations $z=-x$ and $z=x+2.$

questions.problem: Given the elliptic cone $\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}={z}^{2},$ find its intercept with the $z$-axis.
questions.worked_solution:
To find the $z$-intercept of the elliptic cone, we plug $x=0$ and $y=0$ into the equation and solve for $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{0}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{0}^{2}}{9} & ={z}^{2} \\ 0+0 & ={z}^{2} \\ {z}^{2} & =0 \\ z & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intercept with the $z$-axis is $(0,0,0)$ only.

questions.problem: Find the center of the elliptic cone $9(x+3)^{2}+4(y+2)^{2}={z}^{2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The general equation of an elliptic cone with center at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ is

$$
\frac{(x-{x}_{0})^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-{y}_{0})^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=\frac{(z-{z}_{0})^{2}}{{c}^{2}}.
$$

To find the center, we rewrite our equation in standard form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}9(x+3)^{2}+4(y+2)^{2} & =(z-0)^{2} \\ \frac{(x+3)^{2}}{1/9}+\frac{(y+2)^{2}}{1/4} & =(z-0)^{2} \\ \frac{(x-(-3))^{2}}{1/9}+\frac{(y-(-2))^{2}}{1/4} & =(z-0)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of an elliptic cone that has its center at $(-3,-2,0).$

questions.problem: Given that the intersection of the elliptic cone $4(x+3)^{2}+8(y-1)^{2}=(z+7)^{2}$ and the plane $z=-3$ is an ellipse, what is the length of its major axis?
questions.worked_solution:
To find the intersection of the elliptic cone and the plane $z=-3,$ we substitute $z=-3$ into the equation of the elliptic cone, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}4(x+3)^{2}+8(y-1)^{2} & =(-3+7)^{2} \\ 4(x+3)^{2}+8(y-1)^{2} & ={4}^{2} \\ 4(x+3)^{2}+8(y-1)^{2} & =16 \\ \frac{(x+3)^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{2} & =1 \\ \frac{(x+3)^{2}}{(2)^{2}}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{(\sqrt{2})^{2}} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of an ellipse with a semi-major axis of length $a=2.$ Therefore, the major axis has length $2a=4.$
